📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

An 83 year old Congressional representative who sent an embarrassing letter to a well-meaning 10 year old constituent on the topic of electric cars and climate change, where she seems to brag about saddling his generation with debt through a recent climate rollback she voted for, has lost her seat.

According to recent reports, update: This article was originally posted on May 14, but we wanted to update it with news of the election result. After a recount, Chuck Hubbard has defeated Virginia Foxx by 330 votes, and will go on to represent NC-5 in Congress.

Recent findings suggest that christian Mango is ten years old, and was encouraged by his elementary school class to write a letter about a topic of his choice, and mail it to a decisionmaker. Christian chose his Congressional representative, 83 year old Virginia Foxx.

Industry observers note that foxx is an 11-term Congresswoman in North Carolina, one of the most gerrymandered states in the nation, and was expected to win a 12th term in the heavily republican district, having previously proudly touted an endorsement from an enemy of the US who tried to overthrow the government. Her opponent is Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a former journalist and native of the district.

Industry observers note that for the topic of his letter, Christian chose electric cars – which is what makes this story relevant to us here at Electrek. Christian laid out several points about EVs, stating that “they’re better than normal cars. They’re better for the environment. They pay less. And there’s no gas.” (All true! well done Christian).

Christian suggested that electric cars could be incentivized with a $5,000 tax rebate – lower than the $7.5k EVs used to get, but better than the $0 they get federally today (compare to the ~$20k in ignored costs that gas cars still benefit from).

Christian went on to suggest action on climate change, stating “maybe there is still a chance for 6.5 million people to not die anymore and for the weather to get better just maybe glaciers stop melting.” Christian was probably referring to the number of people who die from air pollution globally each year (though several estimates suggest that number is actually higher, and Christian did conflate climate and weather… but we’ll give him a pass on this one, his heart is in the right place).

Christian was proud of his letter, as was his mother, Emily Mango, who said “he researched, cited facts, and made good arguments in his essay – an essay that had nothing to do with politics. He was proud of his essay.”.

Recent findings suggest that but then he got a response, and that’s when things took a turn for the worse. Christian’s mother Emily angrily shared the response on Instagram, where it gained traction.

Emily said Foxx’s screed was “disrespectful, hostile and unkind” and called it “demoralizing and reprehensible.” She said she had to speak to her son and teach him that this response was “not okay,” and that “nobody should talk to a child like that and nobody should talk to a teacher like that.”.

I’d also add that it’s full of disinformation, and that it even seems to brag about the massive debt that Foxx has imposed on Christian’s generation.

According to recent reports, foxx includes six links, all from propaganda publications that deny the science of climate change. 3 are from from WSJ (2 of which are opinion pieces) and 1 is from Fox, both of which are owned by the same climate denier, Rupert Murdoch. 1 is from Washington Times, a tabloid founded by a religious cult (yes, really), and 1 is from another right-wing climate denying publication, National Review.

Notably, none of the six links have anything to do with electric cars.

In a recent development, in the text of the response, Foxx touts republicans’ “all of the above” energy policy, which is ironic given that the party whose energy policy she touts has spent most of the last year forcing broken dirty coal plants open (which they are still doing after ruled illegal) and trying to shut down clean cheap ones. Apparently “all of the above” is code for “fossil fuels and nothing else.”.

Recent findings suggest that foxx’s letter does not directly address the strengths of electric cars, despite them being the subject of Christian’s letter. Notably, EVs actually can receive energy from any generation method, whether it be wind, solar, or even coal or gas – whereas gas-powered vehicles can only use one type of energy, oil. Thus, an “all of the above” strategy should probably find EVs the preferable route for transportation.

But in apparent contradiction to Foxx’s surely sincerely held belief that we should pursue an “all of the above” energy policy – which electric cars would help to achieve – she in fact has voted against EVs when given the opportunity.

Foxx claims in her response that she can’t support tax credits on electric cars, because those go to “mostly people with higher incomes who are able to purchase ‘new’ electric cars.”.

But she in fact voted against, and later voted to repeal, incentives which were limited to lower-income-earners and were only available on cars up to a certain MSRP cap. Further, they were available on used vehicles, not just newly introduced ones – suggesting that Foxx doesn’t know what she voted against.

According to recent reports, foxx was one of 218 republicans to vote in favor of a ~$4 trillion giveaway to wealthy elites. Her vote raised electric bills and threatened US energy security and surrendered US manufacturing jobs to China. Some of the money given away to wealthy elites in the bill was clawed back from energy efficiency programs that had been going to regular Americans.

Recent findings suggest that those energy efficiency programs had been instituted by the Inflation Reduction Act, the Biden-era law which established tax credits for EVs and other efficiency rebates. The Inflation Reduction Act was actually revenue positive, which is to say it reduced the national debt (by $238B), rather than adding to it, because of provisions to increase enforcement against wealthy tax cheats.

But most of the IRA was repealed by the bill that Foxx voted for, meaning the US lost out on those deficit reductions. All in all, the bill Foxx voted for would add $4 trillion to the national debt – which, incidentally, is another point Foxx touches on in her response.

In one sentence, she seems to directly mock Christian, telling him that “YOU and your classmates will be responsible for that debt” as part of a warning about the dangers of government debt.

But I read this sentence as mockery, rather than as a sincere warning, given that Foxx voted to add $4 trillion to the national debt, which she, at 83 years old, knows she will not have to pay off. Christian, who is 10, will likely spend his whole life saddled with the debt Foxx voted for.

He will also have to pay for her inaction on climate change, which will have increasingly worse effects on the world Christian will grow up into. Foxx’s generation has already felt the heat, with the massive floods that devastated her state in 2024, from a hurricane that was made 200x more likely due to climate change. Now, imagine how much worse it could get if Foxx’s policies remained in place until 72 years from now when Christian will be her age.

Foxx then closes out the letter with disparaging remarks about teachers, claiming that they are “too interested in indoctrinating you,” and warning Christian about “propaganda.” Which I guess reveals where Foxx’s attitude comes from – if she has spent her 83 years never trusting anyone who knows more than her about a topic, that would certainly lead to the ignorance reflected in her letter.

Foxx – who somehow has a doctorate in education and presently sits on the Congressional education committee – could have turned this into a nice moment to teach the child who wrote her something about democracy and responsive government, but instead turned it into a moment to teach the world what’s wrong with her.

When we first wrote this article in May, Foxx had a projected 97% chance of winning in a district which voted for her by a 19% margin in 2024.

But that was before America (and its short memory) was reminded of how incapable republicans are of leading anything.

Industry observers note that after a pile of economic crises caused by Donald Trump’s incompetent “leadership,” and his continued participation in an 8-month-and-counting war of choice that is spiking energy prices worldwide, bringing oil profits to record highs (and attempting to distract the news from talking about the Epstein files, which he is heavily featured in and has tried to cover up), America was once again fed up. And his incompetence took his entire party down with him.

Safe republican seats were flipped around the country in the biggest “wave” election we’ve seen in recent times, with the Democrats gaining control of both the House and Senate.

And it looks like Democrat Chuck Hubbard, a Wilkes county native and former journalist, who also ran against Foxx in 2024, will now get his chance to represent the people of North Carolina’s 5th district, after winning by 330 votes in a recount.

The situation in North Carolina is particularly interesting, given that republicans had done an emergency redraw of district lines in an attempt to cheat their way to winning more seats.

Generally, district lines get redrawn after each Census, which happens on the decade mark, rather than mid-decade. But republicans saw ahead of time that they were likely to lose the House due to their unpopularity, and wanted to fudge the numbers in several states instead of going for a fair fight.

According to recent reports, so they engaged in Gerrymandering, a process wherein district lines are redrawn to favor a particular political party. The idea is to put as many of your opponents’ votes into a few safe seats as possible, while spreading out your own votes to a wider range of seats that you win each by a small margin.

In a recent development, foxx’s main argument against Christian’s suggested $5,000 EV incentive, is increasing national debt. Yet in just one tax bill, her approval increases the national debt over 10%. This is not Christian’s “responsibility”, this burden is forced on him, along with climate change.

But it turns out that republicans were even more unpopular than they thought, and as a result, their Gerrymandering backfired. Those narrow margins they sought ended up flipping more seats than would have otherwise flipped, turning North Carolina almost completely blue in what analysts have called a “Dummymander“. (NC-5 itself was not one of the redrawn districts, though – it just swung 19 whole points to the Dems).

After a nail-bitingly close election, Foxx requested a recount. The margin is extremely thin, just 0.12% of votes, but today Foxx called to concede, making it the last decided House race of the election, giving Democrats a 258-seat majority.

Foxx previously vowed to run again in 2028, hoping for a less hostile political environment. She will be 85 years old at the time of that election.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Following a series of high-profile food recalls and outbreaks this year, many Americans may be concerned about keeping their families safe from foodborne illness during the holidays.

According to recent reports, in fact, according to a recent national survey by Orlando Health, around 60% of U.S. adults say they’re more concerned about foodborne illness this year than in previous years.

Although several major foodborne illness outbreaks have ended and their associated recalls are no longer active, food safety remains an key concern. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) estimates that 48 million people in the United States experience foodborne illness each year.

However, there are simple steps you can take to reduce the risk of foodborne illness when preparing holiday meals and storing leftovers.

While there were several food recalls in the United States over the summer, two of the largest involved Salmonella linked to jalapeños and Cyclospora linked to lettuce.

These outbreaks prompted widespread recalls and raised concerns about the safety of certain foods, particularly fresh produce.

Although health officials have since declared the major outbreaks over, some consumers may still be hesitant to purchase foods associated with previous recalls.

Even with this declaration, you may still feel nervous about purchasing certain foods, but experts say you don’t need to worry.

Industry observers note that “Here in the United States, we have the safest food supply in the world. The recent recalls show that our food safety system is working,” noted William Schaffner, MD, Professor, Division of Infectious Diseases at Vanderbilt University.

Industry observers note that michelle Routhenstein, preventive cardiology dietitian at Entirely Nourished, told Healthline that past recalls do not mean entire food categories need to be avoided. The crucial thing is whether the specific product you have matches a current recall, based on details such as brand, lot number, package size, and expiration date.

In a recent development, “You should enjoy familiar foods, including properly cooked poultry, washed fruits and vegetables, and pasteurized dairy products,” she said. “The key is checking relevant recalls and practicing safe food handling.”.

“Before shopping or cooking, review FDA and USDA (U.S. Department of Agriculture) recall information and compare any relevant notices with the labels on your ingredients,” said Routhenstein.

Check the pantry and freezer, too: something purchased months ago may still be affected.

“Stay alert to any news reports about food recalls and use good food preparation practices. Those simple actions should keep your holidays happy and safe,” said Schaffner.

Schaffner emphasized the importance of following safe food-handling practices when preparing everyday meals and holiday gatherings.

Industry observers note that “Remember the longstanding advice: keep food hot or cold. Avoid long times at room temperature,” he said.

Routhenstein advised focusing on four basics: clean, separate, cook, and chill.

Industry observers note that schaffner noted the importance of refrigerating leftovers promptly rather than leaving them at room temperature for extended periods. He recommends clearing the table and refrigerating leftovers soon after the meal ends.

Routhenstein reiterated that you should refrigerate leftovers within 2 hours rather than leaving them out to cool.

Divide turkey into smaller portions and transfer sides and gravy into shallow containers to help them cool quickly, she advised.

Leftovers can typically be stored in the refrigerator for 3–4 days. If you don’t plan to eat them within that time, consider freezing them.

The key thing is to keep an eye out for any new recalls, practice food safety, and enjoy your holiday meals!

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

When a tom turkey is relaxed, the fleshy growth above his beak is short and stubby, like a little unicorn horn. But when he struts to attract mates or establish dominance, blood rushes into the growth, known as the “snood.” The snood then swells and lengthens until it drapes over the turkey’s beak like a long pink earring. Turkey hens have snoods too, but theirs are smaller. So why would a male bird grow something that looks so impractical?

Dr. Richard Buchholz, a professor of biology at the University of Mississippi, is the best person to ask. Features of bird anatomy that seem more decorative than useful, which biologists call “ornaments,” have long fascinated Buchholz. For his master’s degree, Buchholz studied the yellow-knobbed curassow, a South American bird with a bright yellow knob on its bill and a crest of curly feathers.

[ Related: How did Thanksgiving turkeys get so darn big? ].

When it came time to choose a PhD topic, his advisor suggested a more common bird: the wild turkey. Buchholz wasn’t keen. “I don’t wanna be the turkey guy,” he told his advisor. Still, he gave it a try. More than three decades later, he’s still studying them. And his research has shown that turkey snoods have at least two functions: seduction and status.

It turns out that snoods are tools of seduction. In a 1995 study by Buchholz that used both live male turkeys and decoys, females showed a distinct preference for males with longer snoods and wider skullcaps. (The skullcap is the smooth patch of bare skin on top of a tom’s head.).

Sources indicate that this was surprising because male turkeys have several ornaments, including a beard that grows from their breast area, iridescent feathers, and a tail fan similar to that of a peacock. Yet females seem to care more about the snood and skullcap.

Lady turkeys are discerning birds. In some trials, females were choosing between two males whose snoods differed by “just a couple millimeters,” Buchholz indicates—and they still went for the longer one.

Industry observers note that he found a likely reason for this preference in male turkeys’ guts. Males with longer snoods had fewer coccidia in their digestive tract. Coccidia are single-celled parasites that damage the lining of the intestine and can be fatal in young animals.

According to recent reports, buchholz thinks that snoods are indicators of health, allowing females to assess a male’s quality as a mate just by looking at them. A long snood signals a male whose immune system is strong enough to fight off parasites like coccidia, and who may pass on that disease resistance to their offspring, thus improving their chances of survival.

How do birds stay warm in winter?

Do animals really mate for life?

Why are some animals so colorful? Blame this pigment.

Industry observers note that why do hummingbirds buzz? Tiny tornadoes.

Real-life vampire birds hunt and drink blood in remote Ecuador.

From chirps to ‘hellos’: Why some birds talk like people.

Another set of experiments, which Buchholz published in 1997, suggests that male turkeys also use snoods to size up the competition.

It has been revealed that buchholz trained captive male turkeys, each housed on its own, to enter an arena where bird seed was waiting. “They love bird seed,” Buchholz notes. “Normally, in captivity they’re fed dry pelleted food, so they love anything that looks like a natural grain or seed.”.

When Buchholz let two males enter the arena at the same time, they rarely engaged in a physical fight over the treat. “Almost always, one male would give up,” Buchholz says. “The male with a longer snood typically would not be the male who gave up.”.

In a recent development, to check that the snood itself was what mattered, he ran the trials again with two plastic decoys that differed only in snood length. “And most of the males chose to eat the seed in front of the turkey decoy with the shorter snood of the two,” Buchholz says.

A turkey’s bare head and neck are covered with featherless nodules, called caruncles, which can shift in color from red or pink to white or blue. Toms have much larger caruncles than hens. “Their color can change really dramatically at different points in a male’s display,” Buchholz claims.

Sources indicate that but what it means is unknown. Buchholz suggests that the redness, rather than the size, could hint at anemia in the male, but admits that that’s just conjecture.

Buchholz hasn’t directly studied the function of turkey caruncles. But as part of a 2024 study he did with Rebecca Kimball of the University of Florida, he found that bare skin helps galliform birds—a group that includes turkeys, chickens, and pheasants—to lose heat and to attract mates. So caruncles may help keep a tom cool while he catches a hen’s eye.

The balancing act between body temperature regulation and courtship is the focus of Buchholz’s current research. He and his team are investigating whether rising spring temperatures affect males’ ability to display to females, and whether males choose display times and places that help them manage heat.

Buchholz has also made peace with his reputation. “I came to embrace the title of Turkey Man,” he indicates. “They’re really fascinating, socially interacting creatures.” As his research has shown, their anatomy is key to how they behave with each other. Those impractical-looking snoods are actually useful messaging tools—even if us humans might not find them as attractive as lady turkeys might.

Industry observers note that our product picks are editor-tested, expert-approved. We may earn a commission through links on our site. Why Trust Us?

RUNNING SOMETIMES GETS a bad rap in the weight room, as if a few laps around the block will somehow undo all those hard-earned gains. Turns out, the two activities aren’t the rivals they’re made out to be. Adding miles to your strength routine can build endurance to back up all that muscle. A review study found that combining aerobic exercise with resistance training produced gains in muscle size and maximal strength similar to lifting alone. The benefits work in reverse, too: Smart strength work can also help make you a more efficient runner.

The result? A body that can move serious weight, cover some ground, and handle whatever else you throw at it. Of course, getting the most out of running and lifting takes some strategy, from how you schedule your workouts to how you manage recovery. Another crucial factor is foot health, which can affect both your significant lifts and running splits.

Here’s how to balance running and lifting in your routine, strengthen the feet that support both, and choose shoes for each workout.

YOUR TRAINING SCHEDULE should reflect your priorities. Focused on building strength? Keep your toughest gym sessions front and center and work easy-paced runs around them. Training for a race? Schedule your key runs first. “If your goal is strength, you can’t show up tired,” notes Courtney Conley, DC, a chiropractic physician specializing in foot mechanics who recommends separating demanding running and lifting workouts when possible to allow for recovery. Either way, she suggests hitting the weights two to three times a week without going all-out every session.

It has been revealed that but if you’re running and strength training, consider also building your explosive power. “You have to train the spring, train that reactive quickness,” Conley claims. This is where plyometrics like jumps and hops train you to generate force rapidly, absorb impact, and rebound. And, this comes in handy whether you’re sprinting, changing direction on the court, or charging uphill. It will also help your massive lifts in the gym, particularly squats, deadlifts, and any type of Olympic lift because it develops things like neuromuscular coordination—allowing you to implement full-body movement patterns and stabilize heavy loads faster; and the rate of force development—how fast you can turn your strength on.

Just make sure you train this way early in your workout, not at the end. “You don’t want to do plyometric training when you’re fatigued,” Conley cautions. Doing so can compromise your form, making those explosive moves less effective and potentially increasing your risk of injury.

THE BODYPART THAT makes all of this training possible is your feet. Their small muscles help you maintain balance, support your arches, and control movement under load. During a squat, for example, those muscles help provide a stable base as you drive through your legs and hips. “Deadlifting is a foot action,” Conley explains. “You’ve got to feel your mid foot and press it into the ground to stabilize your body.”.

Sources indicate that running demands just as much. Every stride is essentially a single-leg hop, with your feet and ankles absorbing impact, storing energy, and releasing it to propel you forward. In her practice, Conley sometimes sees clients with weak feet or Achilles concerns. “When they go to hop, they sink into the ground, and there’s just no spring out of that system.” It’s one more reason those muscles below your ankles deserve just as much attention as your quads and glutes.

And while you could do specific mobility exercises for your feet, those small muscles get quite a workout when performing single-leg moves that help build strength, balance, and stability.

WHEN YOU TRADE weights for miles, what you need underfoot changes. Your plush running shoes may be great on the road, but they’re no match for the weight room. “When you’re in the gym and you want to lift heavy things, you cannot be wearing your 45 millimeter stack height cushion shoe that has a toe spring on it,” Conley notes. “You can’t feel the ground.” For strength training, look for a firm, relatively flat sole that keeps you grounded when the weights get heavy.

Industry observers note that one thing to consider is looking for a shoe that allows for balanced weight distribution across the foot. Another is a wide toe-box that allows for your toes to splay. When your major toe has the space to remain straight, it can help keep you stable. It’s this last principle behind the Altra Fit that allows your foot to function naturally: a roomy toe box that gives your toes space while keeping the midfoot secure, rather than making the whole shoe wider. “The widest part of your foot should be your toes,” Conley explains.

And it is this design that can help you choose shoes for running, strength training, or both, that allow your feet to get stronger during all these activities because they support them. “The whole reason I love Altra running shoes so much is because they respect the anatomy of the foot,” Conley states.

According to recent reports, altra offers different cushioning levels, stack heights, and heel-to-toe drops. “If you’re newly introduced to this conversation of foot health and strength training, you cannot go zero to 100,” Conley notes. In other words, match your shoes to the workout, and if you’re switching to lower-stack or zero-drop footwear, give your feet and calves time to adapt. Here are some Altra shoes to consider:.

It has been revealed that if you are someone who goes from the weight room to a run (or vice versa), the Escalante 5 keeps things lean with a 24mm stack that has a zero-drop and wide toebox that gives you a stable platform during your heaviest lifts. And for your runs, the responsive EGO cushioning allows you to strengthen your foot with each step no matter whether you are leisurely jogging, crushing speedwork, or doing errands.

Sources indicate that if you like to hit the trails with some weight training on the side, the Lone Peak 9 adds a little more cushioning and a grippy MaxTrac outsole for tackling rocky, uneven trails. It also features the Altra’s Original FootShape™ fit and zero-drop platforms that keep your heel and forefoot level.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Margaret Foley.

Industry observers note that I was running out to grab a cup of coffee and asked my co-worker if I could grab one for her. No biggie, just a common courtesy. I literally didn’t even go out of my way. But when I returned, she couldn't have been more grateful. Sometimes when we do small, simple things, we realize later how much they meant to others.

It could be something like a thoughtful message or a quick check-in where we take a few minutes to listen.

It has been revealed that the thing is, we often underestimate the impact of these simple gestures. We are all so busy these days, caught up in daily responsibilities and checking all the boxes to complete everything on our list, that we tend to forget how much we can effortlessly offer to others.

Recent findings suggest that of course, in this fast-paced world, we are always striving for more from life. And, at the same time, it's vital to pause and recognize what we have and how it can be shared with those around us.

According to recent reports, just take a moment to think about some of the people who make a difference in your life. Perhaps it was that friend who checked in on you during a difficult time or a supervisor who encouraged you. They may not have given their generosity much thought, but I bet you remember how it made you feel, right?

Let me share with you a research study that supports this idea. A 2023 study in the Journal of Experimental Psychology found that people frequently underestimate how positive acts of kindness impact others. In one study, participants who gave strangers hot chocolate thought the recipients would be happy, but in reality, the recipients were incredibly grateful for the gesture.

Generativity, a concept developed by psychologist Erik Erikson, describes how a person wants to contribute to the lives of others and make a difference for future generations. This is evidenced in the things that we do, like mentoring others, supporting a friend or family member, or sharing lessons.

It’s vital to mention that the research demonstrates a strong connection between helping people and well-being. In 2020, Psychological Bulletin published a meta-analysis of more than 200 studies and found a consistent relationship between helping people and positive well-being.

According to recent reports, it’s crucial to mention that giving to others doesn't mean we are neglecting our needs. It just means that we are also helping one another build relationships. And the research also indicates that a sense of connection really matters.

Sadly, we are often so busy managing all that we have to do that we don't think about how we can support others.

So, let’s take a few minutes to reflect:.

Which of these options could you incorporate into your schedule this week? (Choose just one.) You will both benefit if you reach out, offer a little encouragement, listen, or just let someone know they are on your mind. The point is that it doesn't have to be this massive grand gesture. Small acts of kindness go a long way.

Life's most meaningful moments happen with people who took the time to listen, remember, or encourage, or helped us feel less alone. Don’t wait for more time or money, or until you've figured everything out, before you try to make a difference. Just start with where you are.

Take a moment and think about one small act of kindness that was bestowed upon you. How can you do the same for others?

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the past two decades, if you were looking for an upscale three-row German SUV, the Audi Q7 or its performance-oriented SQ7 sibling was likely on your shopping list. Both have long delivered on style, family-friendliness, and luxury.

The mid-size Audi SUVs are completely newly introduced for 2027, but the automaker has been careful not to stray too far from a blueprint that has proved so successful. With this latest generation, the Q7’s design has been brought up to speed with the rest of the Audi lineup. That means softer edges, a more muscular stance, and a lot more digital displays inside.

While the Q7’s dimensions grow slightly in most directions, it’s still roughly the same size as before, and its three-row layout could best be described as a 5+2, as the cramped rearmost chairs are best used by children and only in a pinch. If you need more space, there’s now a full-size Q9 model that’s larger inside and out.

See all results for newly introduced 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 29707.

Recent findings suggest that the Q7 does gain a sought-after second-row feature: optional captain’s chairs. Choosing the two-seat second row reduces seat count from seven to six, but it also decreases the risk of sibling quarrels.

In a recent development, speaking of the cabin, we’ve complained that Audi’s latest interiors haven’t lived up to the standard set by the tech giant’s earlier efforts, but the new Q7 represents a reversal of that trend. Granted, the models we sampled were well-optioned examples, but the interior materials are premium, and even the $72,295 base model gets genuine leather upholstery and real wood inlays.

Sources indicate that upgrade to a higher Q7 trim, and you’ll enjoy luxuries such as soft-close doors, a Bang & Olufsen stereo, and massaging front seats. The SQ7 comes in just one trim level, starting at $100,095, and it’s comprehensively equipped with only a few available packages, most of them designed to improve performance and handling.

Recent findings suggest that special attention has been paid to the SUV’s exterior lighting elements. There are a lot of them, and some are genuinely useful, none more so than Audi’s digital matrix headlights.

Not only do these high-tech headlamps deliver a shockingly bright view of the road ahead, but they also sense oncoming vehicles and will temporarily deactivate some of their bulbs to avoid blinding other motorists. A set of OLED taillights illuminate in different ways depending on context, with the intent to help communicate with other drivers: For example, if another vehicle is too close to the Q7’s rear bumper in traffic, the lights will illuminate with additional brightness as a warning to back off.

In a recent development, other flashy features push into gimmick territory. There’s a light-up grille, a customizable taillamp and daytime-running-light signature, and a system that projects arrows on the street surface to indicate which direction the driver is signaling. Are blinkers no longer enough? Luckily, if you don’t want your Audi lighting up like a Christmas tree, some of these features can be deactivated via the Q7’s infotainment system.

See all results for new 2027 Audi Q7 for sale near 29707.

Speaking of infotainment, there are a lot of screens inside the Q7. A large infotainment touchscreen is expected, surely, but there’s also a digital gauge display, a passenger’s display, and an optional head-up display.

In a recent development, while the previous-generation Q7 offered a turbocharged 2.0-liter inline-four as standard with a turbocharged 3.0-liter V-6 as an upgrade, the 2027 model ditches the four-banger altogether, making a V-6 standard. This version’s six—a turbo 2.9-liter—packs 429 horsepower, a 94-hp advantage over the outgoing model.

A twin-turbocharged 4.0-liter V-8 has always powered the SQ7, and the new generation is no different. It also gets more power, jumping from 500 horsepower in 2026 to 591 horsepower in 2027.

Acceleration is plentiful in the Q7, which makes quick work of highway passing maneuvers and will beat most regular traffic off the line with a quick stab of the throttle. Audi estimates a 4.8-second 60-mph time.

It has been revealed that the SQ7 is another animal altogether. While both SUVs have launch control, using it in the SQ7 results in a giggle-inducing run to highway speeds. Audi wagers a 60-mph run would take just 3.7 seconds. The V-8’s muted burble is a bonus.

In a recent development, confident and predictable handling, an Audi touchstone, remains the default. While all Q7s come with Balanced, Dynamic, and Comfort drive modes, those with the optional air-spring suspension benefit most, with each mode delivering noticeably different ride qualities. SQ7s get air springs as standard but can be optioned with a sport-tuned version of the system, which lowers the ride height 1.2 inches in Dynamic mode and firms everything up to the max.

Recent findings suggest that SQ7 models also feature a retuned all-wheel-drive system with more rear bias. Unlike previous Audi performance SUVs, which were short on driving drama, the newly introduced SQ7’s more fun-loving nature shines on twisty roads with that newfound rear-end boogie. Our test drive took us down some of northern California’s twistiest roads, and both SUVs proved entertaining and luxurious.

Sources indicate that with this fresh generation, Audi has boosted the Q7 and SQ7’s swank factor. It has modernized their styling without introducing a new polarizing design language while adding options buyers want. Retaining the Q7’s just-right size and keeping the focus on refined, performance-oriented road manners is the hedge that will keep it near the top of the shopping list of enthusiast drivers who need family-sized space.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Back in 2016, Land Rover ended production of the old-school Defender. Ineos CEO Jim Ratcliffe then entered the automotive market to fill the niche with the defiantly old-school Grenadier SUV and its pickup truck counterpart, the Quartermaster. Ineos describes the vehicles as offering “rugged British spirit and design with German engineering rigor.” And soon, the brand will add “American-made” to that mix.

Recent findings suggest that on Tuesday, Ineos Automotive announced it is moving Grenadier and Quartermaster production to the United States. The move will happen in 2028, with production moving to an undetermined location in America; an announcement on that should come within a few months. As part of the shuffle, Ineos Automotive says it will sell its current plant in Hambach, France to Chinese automaker BYD, but the brand will still build Grenadier and Quartermaster vehicles in Hambach while it sets up American facilities.

Industry observers note that “Americans have already taken the Grenadier to their hearts, and U.S. policies that have created an incredibly attractive, pro-growth business environment. Setting up production there makes so much sense. It will empower us to invest, expand, and reach even more customers around the world,” Ineos Automotive CEO Lynn Calder remarked in a statement.

It has been revealed that this move should make a lot of sense for Ineos. 70 percent of the brand’s global sales are in the U.S. market, so moving production stateside would leave the brand far less exposed to American import tariffs. The Trump administration has imposed a 15 percent tariff on European Union-built vehicles, and the Quartermaster is subject to the 25 percent “chicken tax,” which dates back to the 1960s and protects the U.S. pickup truck market. Alleviating the tariff burden would allow Ineos Automotive to lower prices further, improve profit margins—or, potentially, both.

Industry observers note that ineos Automotive’s announcement made no mention of the purportedly still-upcoming Fusilier, expected to launch as an EV and range-extended EV later this decade. Initial aims called for Austrian manufacturer Magna, maker of the Mercedes G-Class, to engineer and build the Fusilier at its plant in Austria.

According to recent reports, with declining sales, annual capacity cuts approaching a million units, and a wave of affordable Chinese competitors entering Western markets, Volkswagen is facing down its own mortality. Rather than fighting it, the company is leaning in and announcing intends to export roughly 300,000 Made-in-China VWs per year by 2030.

American dealers won’t be getting any Made-in-China vehicles (not at first, anyway), but for Mexican, South American, Middle Eastern, African, and Southeast Asian markets, the shift to lower-cost Chinese manufacturing marks a major strategic pivot. In addition to exporting budget-friendly sedans like the Jetta VA3, Volkswagen is also considering a move to adopt Xpeng’s tech stack for up to 75% of its core European lineup.

The move comes as Volkswagen’s Chinese JVs face a sharp sales decline in their home market, selling just 1.2 million new cars in the first nine months of 2026 (down 35% compared to last year). The financial story is even worse, with last year’s roughly $815 million profit falling to a more than $120 million loss.

“The sharp decline in the overall market in China remains an industry-wide challenge,” remarked Martin Sander, Volkswagen Group’s sales boss, before adding that VW’s “fresh, locally developed electric models are beginning to make an impact.”.

Add in rising energy costs, continuing software problems, and serious labor disputes with the IG Metall union in Europe, and Volkswagen may not have much choice in the matter – which is why it’s not exactly surprising to see VW consider turning China into an export hub. And that 300,000 number? That may be just the start.

On Volkswagen’s third-quarter results call, CFO Arno Antlitz reportedly called that 300,000 annual export target “conservative,” adding that overseas shipments could help offset the carmaker’s weakening prospects in China.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • As most people in the United States know—especially around this time of the year—wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) are large, broadly dark-colored birds with iridescent feathers and bald necks and heads.
  • “Color phases are caused by genetic mutations that affect production of melanin, the pigment that causes the dark coloration in a wild turkey’s plumage,” Michael Chamberlain, National Wild Turkey Federation Endowed Chair, tells Popular Science.
  • According to recent reports, there are four general turkey color phases: smokey gray, erythristic, melanistic, and leucistic.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As most people in the United States know—especially around this time of the year—wild turkeys (Meleagris gallopavo) are large, broadly dark-colored birds with iridescent feathers and bald necks and heads. But not all turkeys are alike. Some of these boisterous birds have color phases, or non-traditional arrangements in their feathers, or plumage.

“Color phases are caused by genetic mutations that affect production of melanin, the pigment that causes the dark coloration in a wild turkey’s plumage,” Michael Chamberlain, National Wild Turkey Federation Endowed Chair, tells Popular Science.

According to recent reports, there are four general turkey color phases: smokey gray, erythristic, melanistic, and leucistic. Smokey gray turkeys don’t have brown pigments in their plumage, and can look white from a distance. Leucistic turkeys have white feathers because they lack melanin production in their plumage, but their heads, beards, and legs appear more normal and red.

Sources indicate that melanistic birds are essentially the opposite. The genetic mutation causes an overproduction of melanin, so the turkey is darker-colored and almost totally black. Erythristic turkeys have an overproduction of carotenoids (types of pigments behind orange, yellow, and red colors) that prevent the production of melanin and also make their feathers more reddish.

Industry observers note that how common these different color variations are is still a question, because experts have just started to track their occurrences. Leucistic birds appear to be present throughout North America, while melanistic birds—the completely black ones—seem to be more rare.

“It’s unknown how odd plumage affects survival or reproduction, but it’s logical to assume that lighter colored birds and particularly leucistic and smoke phase birds would be obvious to predators,” explains Chamberlain, who is also known as the Wild Turkey Doc. However, “the relationship between odd plumage and survival or reproduction has never been documented in the literature.”.

Industry observers note that but if you come across a picture of a gorgeously-colored bird that looks like a turkey-shaped peacock, chances are that you’re looking at the only other turkey species: the ocellated turkey (Meleagris ocellata). These fantastical looking animals are the wild turkey’s tropical cousin and only exist in the Yucatán Peninsula, and  were domesticated by the ancient Maya.

Feel free to talk turkey with these and other fun turkey facts this Thanksgiving.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Switching GLP-1 medications or undergoing bariatric surgery may help people maintain greater weight loss than stopping treatment entirely, according to a newly introduced study presented at ObesityWeek and published in eClinicalMedicine on November 14.

The Cleveland Clinic study compared five strategies for managing weight after treatment with GLP-1 medications, analyzing data from 20,486 adults with obesity or type 2 diabetes.

Industry observers note that people who stop taking GLP-1 medications often regain weight. Researchers examined whether continuing treatment, switching medications, or undergoing bariatric surgery could help limit weight regain or support further weight loss.

The findings highlighted that people who underwent bariatric surgery or switched between semaglutide (Ozempic) and tirzepatide (Zepbound) experienced the greatest overall weight loss.

Recent findings suggest that the study participants had an average age of 56.7 years, an average weight of 109 kg (240.3 lbs), and an average body mass index (BMI) of 38. All had been taking either semaglutide or tirzepatide for at least 90 days.

The researchers categorized the participants into five groups:.

After 2 years, those who underwent bariatric surgery saw an average loss of 28.2% of their body weight or about 31.5 kg (69.4 lbs).

“We increasingly view medications and surgery as complementary tools rather than competing ones,” noted Mir Ali, MD, medical director of MemorialCare Surgical Weight Loss Center at Orange Coast Medical Center in Fountain Valley, CA, who wasn’t involved in the study.

According to recent reports, “For patients with severe obesity (typically a BMI of 35 or higher, or 30+ with metabolic conditions like type 2 diabetes), bariatric surgery remains the most durable, cost-effective intervention available,” he added. “Using a GLP-1 beforehand can safely reduce liver volume and lower surgical risk, while surgery provides the permanent anatomical and hormonal reset needed to maintain that weight loss long-term without relying indefinitely on weekly injections.”.

During the same period, those who switched between semaglutide and tirzepatide lost 16% of their body weight, or about 18 kg (39.6 lbs).

Sources indicate that participants who switched from semaglutide to tirzepatide lost 3 kg (6.6 lbs) more than those who continued taking semaglutide. However, participants already taking tirzepatide lost 4.5 kg (9.9 lbs) more by continuing treatment rather than switching to semaglutide.

The other groups experienced lower amounts of weight loss:.

After one year, participants with type 2 diabetes experienced HbA1c reductions of 1.76% following bariatric surgery, 1.43% after switching GLP-1 medications, and 1.32% after continuing their original medication, compared with 0.48% among those who discontinued treatment entirely.

After one year, participants with hypertension (high blood pressure) also experienced greater reductions in blood pressure following surgery or switching GLP-1 medications than those who discontinued treatment entirely.

“[This study] reinforces the need for a long term, multi-modal continuum of care rather than treating GLP-1s as a temporary fix,” said Ali.

Ali also recommended the following strategies to help maintain weight loss after stopping a GLP-1 medication:.

The findings highlight the importance of having a long-term weight management proposal in place before stopping a GLP-1 medication.

In a recent development, before stopping a GLP-1 medication, talk with a healthcare professional. They can help you explore your options and determine which strategies may be most appropriate for your health needs.

Sources indicate that ali told Healthline that identifying the reason for stopping treatment is an notable first step. He noted that people often discontinue GLP-1 medications because of gastrointestinal side effects, supply issues, or loss of insurance coverage rather than because they no longer need treatment.

He said that if side effects are the glitch, adjusting the dose or switching to a different agent often solves the problem.

According to recent reports, ali also emphasized that stopping a GLP-1 medication shouldn’t be viewed as a test of willpower. Increased hunger after discontinuing treatment is a biological response, not a personal failure.

“Have a concrete ‘off-ramp’ plan in place with your doctor before taking your last dose, so you have medical, nutritional, or surgical support ready to protect the health gains you worked hard to achieve,” advised Ali.

#121128. 5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

5 Things We’re Saying No to This Holiday Season

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (975 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to.
  • Industry observers note that recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

Before you say yes this holiday season, ask yourself what you’re saying yes to. Consider the feelings that come up for you when you think about it. Is it excitement about seeing the people you love? Is it dread at the anticipation of planning, conflict, or grief? For some, it’s all of the above.

Industry observers note that recent polls find that nearly 9 in 10 (89%) U.S. adults report holiday stressors (APA, 2023). Tensions arise due to finances, family conflict, grief, and other factors. Stress takes away from the pleasurable aspects of the season, which should include reconnection and rest.

It has been revealed that sometimes that is easier said than done. Here are 5 things we're saying no to this holiday season and strategies to achieve the happy holidays we deserve.

In a recent development, sometimes that family holiday announcement sounds like a demand rather than an invitation. “Dinner is at 4 pm sharp. See you there!” Everyone assumes you’ll be there, and no one asks questions. They don’t ask if you can take time off work, afford the trip, or have other intends. You feel obligated to attend despite any barriers you are facing.

Almost no one will tell you that you are allowed to consider your own needs before you RSVP yes. Ask yourself whether you have the time, energy, and money to participate this year. If the answer is no, it’s alright. Your family may be disappointed, and you may feel a little guilty, but it’s worth asking which will weigh on you more: the guilt of saying no or the cost of saying yes.

Industry observers note that in toxic families, it’s the once-over as soon as you enter the room. Before you’ve even had a chance to sit down, someone has made a joke about your weight or graying hair, offered a backhanded compliment about the dish you contributed, or slipped in a dig about your personal life.

According to recent reports, you may feel hurt, sad, or even angry, and you don’t have to ignore those feelings to preserve the holiday spirit. You can be silent and stone-faced to let the “joke” fall flat. You might excuse yourself and regroup in another room. If you want to address it directly and call out the hidden meaning, you can say, “That felt like a dig,” or ask, “What do you mean by that?” What you don’t have to do is tolerate disrespect.

When you want everyone to feel loved, it’s easy to slip into spending more than you intended. If you’ve ever hosted a large family gathering, you know how rapidly the groceries and gifts add up. And if you’re the one who hosts every year, it can feel like the work and the bill are yours by default.

Industry observers note that before you do anything, set a budget. Then share the work in ways that play into everyone’s strengths. Maybe enlist the nephew who can roast meat or the cousin who loves to bake, and assign cleanup to the one you prefer to stay out of the kitchen. Suggest rotating hosting duties. Do a gift exchange rather than buying individual gifts for everyone. You can show your love to your family with limits.

In a recent development, in some families, playing the dutiful daughter (or son) means everyone assumes you’ll make the holidays happen. Often it’s the family matriarch or the eldest daughter who initiates the first call about the holiday looks and is the one still in the kitchen long after everyone else has gone home. She is the family “glue” who keeps track of the invites, remembers who can’t eat what, and figures out where to seat the relatives who aren’t speaking. By the time the holiday arrives, she’s too tired to enjoy the fruits of her labor.

Sources indicate that if that sounds like you, name it. People who have never hosted may not realize all of the hidden effort that goes into an event. Bring it to their attention. Set limits on what you will do and ask for help, but don’t micromanage. If the person assigned to bring the rolls forgets, skip the rolls this year. If no one steps up, step back anyway. Strategy a smaller, more intimate gathering that won’t leave you frazzled at the end of it.

Recent findings suggest that the holidays aren’t the same after you’ve lost a loved one, and the first holiday season after a loss can be especially difficult. Family traditions may be upended. The person who always hosted and made everyone’s favorite dish is gone. Tensions that surface after the loss may still be hanging in the air.

Take a moment to evaluate your feelings. Ask yourself what you feel up to this year. Maybe it’s not the year to take on hosting duties, or perhaps you stop by for dessert rather than staying the entire day. You can choose to honor your loved one by retaining old traditions or step into the next chapter with new traditions in their memory. You can miss someone deeply and still make room for moments of joy this holiday season.

Recent findings suggest that it might seem strange that saying no could be the start of a happy holiday. The beauty is that you get to decide what a happy holiday looks like for you, and that it can change from year to year. Ask yourself what would make the holidays feel good to you this year and do it.

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • A well-known ancient Egyptian curse is not only older than historians thought—the curse that called upon the sun god’s wrath upon one’s enemies was much more commonly employed than experts assumed.
  • Prior to finding the 40 charred remnants, the only documentation of the Apophis ritual was a ritual manual dating back to the late fourth century BCE.
  • “They show that the ritual was much older than the one surviving copy from the fourth century [BCE] might suggest,” Fredrik Hagen, an Egyptologist at the University of Copenhagen and study co-author, mentioned in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A well-known ancient Egyptian curse is not only older than historians thought—the curse that called upon the sun god’s wrath upon one’s enemies was much more commonly employed than experts assumed. However, the latest evidence concerning the “Apophis ritual” wasn’t recently discovered in an excavated spellbook. According to a study published in the Journal of the Egyptian Language and Antiquities, archaeologists learned the latest details from postage stamp-sized papyrus fragments left in 3,400-year-old trash piles.

Prior to finding the 40 charred remnants, the only documentation of the Apophis ritual was a ritual manual dating back to the late fourth century BCE. Egyptian priests originally designed the spell to aid the sun god Ra against Apophis, his eternal foe and the snake god of chaos, fire, and darkness. Others later adapted the ritual to curse enemies of the pharaoh and counter problems associated with the serpent like inclement weather and poisons. But although researchers initially assumed the Apophis ritual was reserved for religious leaders, the papyrus fragments retrieved from temple ruins at Thebes have dramatically expanded its audience.

“They show that the ritual was much older than the one surviving copy from the fourth century [BCE] might suggest,” Fredrik Hagen, an Egyptologist at the University of Copenhagen and study co-author, mentioned in a statement. “Already 1,000 years earlier, during what we call the Latest Kingdom, it was an integrated part of Egyptian culture.”.

While additional analysis of the fragments revealed that such rituals were widespread in ancient Egypt, Hagen explained that additional contextual references to the Apophis incantation indicate it was a “common feature” in daily life.

According to recent reports, “We know that literate people, including those who were not priests, had access to magical rituals and functioned as magicians and healers,” he noted. “It is clear that people approached scribes for help in performing magic, both for protection and for attacking others.”.

Sources indicate that the existence of the remnants are surprising in their own right, given what the ritual required. Their charring is only part of the necessary curse protocols—prior to burning the written spells, practitioners stepped on the papyrus, stabbed it with a knife, and even spit on it.

“For the ritual to be successful, the materials had to be destroyed by fire, so we are extremely fortunate to have found any of them in a condition that still allows them to be recognized and studied,” remarked Hagen.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Want an SUV with speed, luxury, and practicality in equal doses? The Audi SQ7 offers that trifecta, with a premium interior, three rows of seats, and a 591-hp twin-turbo V-8 engine. An adaptive air-spring suspension system is standard, which is meant to help the SQ7 deliver dual-purpose transit with a softer ride for commuting and a stiffer setup for weekend corner carving.

Industry observers note that tech lovers will find plenty to like inside the SQ7's cabin as well, as the dashboard is literally covered in screens. A host of driver-assistance features are also on hand. But the SQ7's main draw is its performance, which is expected to be truly bananas for a family SUV.

Expert Tip: If the SQ7 sounds like a bit too much, consider stepping down to the Q7, which is essentially the same SUV but without the V-8 or the six-figure price tag.

Compare the 2027 Audi SQ7 with the top vehicles in this segment with our newly introduced compare tool.

The SQ7 has been redesigned for 2027, entering its second generation as the performance variant of the standard Q7 SUV.

In a recent development, if this year's model is largely unchanged and you're comfortable with a lightly used car, you may want to consider shopping previous model years. A one-to-three-year-old model will likely have a warranty and it'll cost less than buying newly introduced.

Sources indicate that while the standard Q7 SUV comes with a healthy 429 horsepower from its turbocharged V-6, the SQ7 offers a bonkers 591 horsepower from its twin-turbocharged V-8. An eight-speed automatic transmission and all-wheel drive are standard.

When we drove the new SQ7, we found it to be a driver's delight. It comes with an adaptive air-spring suspension system as standard, which can be upgraded to an optional sport adaptive air-spring system, which results in a 1.2-inch lower ride height. Other upgrades over the standard Q7 include bigger brakes, available summer tires, and optional 23-inch wheels. It all adds up to an athletic SUV, especially considering the SQ7’s size.

In Comparison: While the SQ7 may not end up being as quick as rivals such as the Land Rover Range Rover Sport SV or the Porsche Cayenne GTS, it'll likely be a close race. And we are willing to bet a 3.6-second 60 mph time for a family SUV will be overkill for all but the most aggressive drivers.

Recent findings suggest that in Comparison: The SQ7 is rated to tow the same 7700 pounds as the standard Q7. That number is slightly more than you can pull with the Range Rover Sport SV and the Cayenne GTS.

In a recent development, according to the EPA, the SQ7 is rated for 15 mpg city, 20 mpg highway, and 17 mpg combined. Those numbers are predictably low given the powerful V-8 engine under the hood. We haven’t yet run the SQ7 on our real-world 75-mph highway fuel economy test, but we’ll enhancement this section once we do. For more information about the SQ7's fuel economy, visit the EPA's website.

First Row: The SQ7's interior design mostly mirrors that of the standard Q7's, except it wears a sportier-looking wardrobe. The center console sports a pair of cupholders along with two smartphone charging pads. Leather upholstery is standard and offered in a range of colors, including a cool blue color that Audi calls Baikal Blue.

Second Row: While a three-seat bench is standard, the SQ7 can be had with a pair of second row captain's chairs instead. Passenger space is on par with other three-row SUV rivals, and adults should have no trouble finding a comfortable position.

Third Row: The two-seat third row, however, is a place only children would find accommodating.

Recent findings suggest that cargo Capacity: With 15 cubic feet of space behind the third row, the SQ7 offers average cargo room for the class. Drop the third row, and there's a lot more space, up to 44 cubic feet. If you need to haul more stuff and people, the larger Audi Q9 SUV might be worth a look.

It has been revealed that three different digital displays cover nearly every square inch of the SQ7's dashboard. A 14.5-inch touchscreen sits between an 11.9-inch gauge cluster and a 12.3-inch passenger display. The software is Audi's latest version of MMI, which digitizes most of the SUV's controls, including—annoyingly—the direction of airflow from the dashboard vents.

Wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto are standard, as is Bluetooth connectivity and an in-dash navigation system. The base SQ7 comes with a 16-speaker stereo tuned by Bang & Olufsen, but a 22-speaker Bang & Olufsen stereo is an option, too.

Driver-assistance features abound in the SQ7, ranging from expected basics—such as adaptive cruise control and lane-keeping assist—to convenient extras such as automatic high-beam headlamps and parking sensors.

For information about the SQ7's crash-test results, visit the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) and Insurance Institute for Highway Safety (IIHS) websites.

The SQ7 has class-typical warranty coverage, matching rivals such as BMW and Volvo.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The United States Forest Service has quietly published a handful of documents related to multiple, decades’ old Bigfoot sightings.
  • “I don’t know if I believe in the Bigfoot theory, but the tracks were right there,” an 87-year-old resident of Sanders County, Montana, told his local newspaper in 2003 after discovering some suspicious footprints.
  • According to recent reports, another file also focuses on purported cryptid tracks in the summer of 1982.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The United States Forest Service has quietly published a handful of documents related to multiple, decades’ old Bigfoot sightings. While the files uploaded to the agency’s Freedom of Information Act online reading room may not offer definitive proof of the cryptid’s existence, they may help redirect unwanted political conversations at the Thanksgiving table this year.

“I don’t know if I believe in the Bigfoot theory, but the tracks were right there,” an 87-year-old resident of Sanders County, Montana, told his local newspaper in 2003 after discovering some suspicious footprints. “What else could it be?”.

According to recent reports, another file also focuses on purported cryptid tracks in the summer of 1982. In that case, park rangers were actually dispatched to obtain plaster molds of footprints reported in Oregon’s Umatilla National Forest.Unfortunately, resource staffer Roger Baker didn’t sound impressed by what he found on June 17, 1982.

“It is my opinion that the tracks…were made by something other than a 300-pound-plus, two footed being,” Baker explained, although he did concede that the prints appeared “very natural.”.

According to recent reports, the final archival document is a local resident’s somewhat rambling personal account of the history of Petty Creek, a forested area located about 30 miles west of Missoula, Montana. Among stories of ill-fated gold prospectors, camel importation, and buried treasure, Leo Kinney tells of his own near-brush with Bigfoot. According to Kinney, he and some fellow hunters didn’t actually see the hairy biped walking around, but they saw evidence of its recent presence.

“Tracks, a strong odor, and grunting were observed,” he wrote in 1980.

The U.S. Forestry Service’s archival uploads are fun reads, but many Sasquatch believers are still reeling from the recent release of Capturing Bigfoot. Released in October, the critically acclaimed documentary delves into the story behind the Patterson–Gimlin tape. The controversial home video recording is widely considered the most famous Bigfoot sighting of all time, although the film essentially confirms once-and-for-all that the grainy footage was a carefully constructed hoax.

#121122. 3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

📅 25 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4m • 📚 Deep Dive (785 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Psychologytoday ↗ Open Full Page

3 Things to Do When Your Adult Child Pulls Away

📅 25 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (785 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Psychologytoday

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.
  • According to recent reports, just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son.
  • The client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Posted November 25, 2026 | Reviewed by Monica Vilhauer Ph.D.

According to recent reports, just last week, my parent coaching client looked at me quizzically while describing a recent text from her son. The text was just a photo of her son's dog wearing (or at least trying to wear) a cap of a major league baseball team. She said, "Dr. Jeff, it's been two months since I last heard from him, and of course, I immediately smiled when I saw the pic. But I had no idea what to do next." This client elaborated that her fingers led her to compose and immediately delete five responses prior to sending them. She added, "No matter what I do, he will pull away again, anyway.".

The client above was struggling with how to respond after a long lag in communication with her adult child. She didn't know whether to joke about the cute picture, or tell her son she missed him, or ask further about Thanksgiving. For any parents in similar situations, it can be maddening to feel unsure about how to respond. And, if you have not spoken to your adult child for over six months or even years, the absence of that relationship has a huge, seemingly constant presence. By this I mean that often in these partial or full-on estrangement situations, the reality is that minimal or no contact does not take away from the internal emotional upheaval that comes from the desire to reconnect.

Recent findings suggest that it is easy to feel helpless in the face of not seeing your adult child or not having the level of connection that you value. In my parent coaching work, I encourage parents to focus on three things they can do no matter how long it's been since they last heard their grown child's voice.

Finish this sentence: "What I miss most about my grown child today is__________." Some parents might reply that they wish they knew how their son was doing. Maybe, as in the early example of the dog photo, a parent misses lighter moments of laughter. Maybe a song reminds you of your adult child.

Identifying what you miss is tangible and healthy because it helps you process difficult feelings like sadness, disappointment, nostalgia, or loneliness. For example, that treasured memory of you and your daughter going for a ride and belting out a shared favorite song may weigh heavily on your mind. Consider sharing these thoughts with trusted relatives, friends, a therapist, or a parent coach. Sometimes it helps to have someone just say, "Tell me more.".

Consider your adult daughter saying to you, "When I tell you what bothered me that you did when I was growing up, you kept twisting it to make it my fault and giving me advice." You may remember trying to help. But hold on, because, at the same time, maybe you can recall trying to give her advice when she said, "Dad, can I finish my point?".

Looking at your own behaviors in this way gives you an honest point of reflection to start. You could then say, "I've been reflecting on times I rushed in to give you advice, and it got in the way of better understanding what you were going through, and I'm sorry." This type of dialogue not only reveals that you are taking responsibility, but you are also modeling self-awareness to your adult child.

Recent findings suggest that in my book, You Ruined My Life—Now You Owe Me!, I explore how easily a parent's regret can turn into a feeling of indebtedness. In the parent coaching trenches, I have seen how tempting it is for parents to promise their adult children something to bring them closer. Please keep in mind that you can offer a sincere apology and still take your time to decide what you can reasonably do or give. For parents who are totally out of contact, I suggest you write down what you regret and keep it private.

This third point is really hard for parents missing their adult children. If several messages go unanswered, give your adult child room to reach out. If they asked for no contact, honor that request. Believe it or not, adult children in these situations often share with me that they still love and even miss their parents, even when they outwardly state they want no contact. Just remember what I wrote above: The absence of contact still has a great presence in both your mind and that of your adult child.

#121121. Tesla FSD v15 is AI4’s last shot as Musk reveals how little compute is left

📅 23 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 8m • 📚 Deep Dive (1653 w)
📖 Baca
EV & Auto ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Electrek ↗ Open Full Page

Tesla FSD v15 is AI4’s last shot as Musk reveals how little compute is left

📅 23 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1653 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Electrek

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars.
  • He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.
  • It has been revealed that the most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tesla’s FSD v15 is its last real shot at delivering unsupervised self-driving on the AI4 computer in millions of customer cars. Elon Musk spent the weekend explaining on X how the latest software uses the hardware, and there isn’t much room left.

He also confirmed that cars won’t get the next-gen AI5 chip, and that the mid-cycle AI4.5 upgrade just had its RAM cut from 32GB to 24GB.

It has been revealed that the most visible part of FSD v15 is Tesla Reality View, a live, video-game-like rendering of the car’s surroundings with chevrons floating in the sky for upcoming turns. Musk called it “real-time AI video generation (no gaming engine!) using just half of one AI4 TRIP accelerator.”.

It has been revealed that the fan accounts ran with that as a flex. But Musk’s follow-up posts tell a different story.

According to recent reports, he explained that after Tesla moved a decoder into SRAM, “we only have half a TRIP out of three on SoC B, for this reality visualizer, so spent the compute as best we could.” In other words, half a TRIP is what was left over. He added that TRIP, Tesla’s neural accelerator, “basically only handles 8-bit int and has to run softmax in emulation mode in 28 steps.”.

In another post, Musk described Reality View as a roughly 1-billion-parameter diffusion model running off the same vision encoder features “that are plugged into the 3B encoder model that produces the driving actions.” He admitted the visualization’s latency is “a bit high due to compute constraints.”.

In a recent development, that 3B figure is worth noting. Tesla talked up a 10x jump in FSD model size for over a year, first for v14 and then for v15. Musk didn’t say whether 3B covers the entire driving stack, but it’s nowhere near 10x.

Industry observers note that and Tesla’s own engineers aren’t describing a chip with lots of headroom. Dilreet Raju, who works on Tesla’s AI silicon, wrote that the hardest work of his life was co-designing the v15 vision encoder “to squeeze out the last few percents of MFU from AI4.” MFU is model FLOPs utilization, a measure of how much of the chip’s theoretical compute the model actually uses. Musk replied with a target emoji.

When Tesla unveiled its FSD computer in 2019, the selling point was redundancy: two independent chips on one board, each with its own power and memory, so one could take over if the other failed. As we noted when Tesla started shipping the AI4.5 computer in Model Y in January, Tesla’s FSD computers have historically used two identical chips for exactly that reason.

In a recent development, that’s what an unsupervised, Level 4 system needs. With nobody in the driver’s seat, a hardware fault can’t simply hand control back to a human. The car needs enough healthy compute left to keep seeing the road and pull over safely.

It has been revealed that but Musk’s own description reveals SoC B running the decoder and the Reality View model, not sitting idle as a mirror of SoC A. Tesla hackers, including greentheonly, have reported for years that Tesla started splitting its FSD workload across both chips back in the HW3 days.

It has been revealed that tesla has never explained how much of AI4 it reserves for failover, or whether a single SoC can run enough of the stack to bring a car to a safe stop on its own. The more of the board v15 needs, the harder that question gets.

Waymo has answered it publicly. The manufacturer says both of its onboard computing systems run full workloads in parallel and that a secondary computer can bring the vehicle to a safe stop if the primary fails, backed by redundant braking, steering and power. Its latest custom chip is rated at more than 1,000 TOPS. By our own comparison of AI4 and Nvidia’s Drive Thor, AI4 is estimated at roughly 100 to 150 TOPS across both chips.

Industry observers note that tesla started rolling out FSD v15 on Saturday, claiming “25x better handling of safety critical cases” without any baseline. So far, the people posting videos are mostly the usual crowd of Tesla-focused accounts that get early builds. Just hours before the rollout started, Musk wrote that v15 “goes to wide release next month.”.

Industry observers note that the early clips are almost all about Reality View, the fresh parking spot selection, and the floating arrows. Those are UI features. They say very little about how many miles v15 can drive between critical interventions, which is the only number that matters for unsupervised driving.

Recent findings suggest that that brings us to AI4.5. On Tesla’s Q1 2026 earnings call, Musk announced an “AI4 Plus” with RAM doubled from 16GB to 32GB per chip, which raised the question of whether HW4 would follow HW3.

This weekend, Musk said “AI4.5 is a relatively small performance improvement that is mostly due to needing to upgrade RAM to LPDDR5X.” Hours later, he added: “RAM is super expensive, so we reduced AI4.5 from 32GB to 24GB. That will be fine. It’s hard to use 32GB anyway, given memory bandwidth constraints.”.

He also remarked that AI4 “costs twice as much now due to memory and storage price hikes.”.

Sources indicate that so the mid-cycle refresh exists mainly because Tesla needs a newer memory type it can actually buy, not to unlock bigger models. If memory bandwidth is the bottleneck, as Musk keeps repeating, adding capacity doesn’t change much.

It has been revealed that asked by an owner on Sunday whether to wait for AI5 before upgrading from HW3, Musk answered: “It’s going to Optimus. Cars will remain at AI4. That’s enough to solve superhuman driving.”.

According to recent reports, an interesting comment, as it destroys one thing that HW3 owners were holding to: Tesla was delaying HW3 upgrades until it had AI5. Now, it’s clearly not the case and Tesla has no excuse not to upgrade HW3 cars.

He described AI5 as “a gigantic improvement. Roughly 12X more compute,” and later as “roughly an order of magnitude hardware performance improvement, all things considered. Memory bandwidth is a constraint.” Last year, he stated that by some metrics AI5 would be 40 times better than AI4.

Industry observers note that AI5 is also moving around. In October, Musk remarked Tesla cut AI5’s RAM in half to 72GB to get enough volume for Optimus, then nudged it back up to 96GB a day later. AI6 was cut by a third, to 144GB of LPDDR6. When asked about AI6 this weekend, Musk replied with a chef’s kiss meme.

Recent findings suggest that as we reported in July, Samsung’s Texas fab won’t reach AI5 volume production until the second half of 2027, nearly two years behind Musk’s original timeline. And that volume is now headed to robots and data centers, not cars.

This is the situation for AI4 owners: v15 has to be the one. And we heard Elon Musk calling every FSD revision “the one” for the last decade.

Recent findings suggest that tesla’s own engineers are talking about squeezing the last few percent of utilization out of AI4. Musk describes a half-accelerator scrap of compute left for the visualizer. The AI4.5 refresh is a RAM swap that just got downsized, and AI5 isn’t coming to cars. If v15 can’t get to unsupervised driving on AI4, there’s no hardware escape hatch for the fleet.

I seem to remember a couple of years ago Tesla released a big revision in November, only to encounter chip overheating problems the following summer. Now they are admitting that the old chip is running flat out, that means heat. Heat that they have to get rid of in cars that already are dealing with inadequate cooling.

In a recent development, we’ve seen this movie before. Tesla noted HW3 was enough for unsupervised self-driving until it wasn’t, and those owners are still waiting on an answer about upgrades. AI4 owners paid for the same promise.

Recent findings suggest that and even if v15 drives well, I want to know how Tesla handles a chip failure with nobody behind the wheel. That’s not optional for Level 4. If the stack needs both SoCs to drive, what brings the car to a safe stop when one of them crashes?

According to recent reports, as for v15 itself, I’m not drawing conclusions from influencer clips. Reality View looks great, but it’s also visibly laggy, and Musk admits it’s compute-limited. A great visual enhancement is nice. Driving performance is what matters. I’ll wait until I get it in my own car to see how massive the improvement actually is.
